scenes.title: When to Question
scenes.summary: Interrogation is opportune when one more question exposes an absurdity, as Pericles asked Lampon about the rites and Socrates asked Meletus whether daimones are children of gods; when the opponent can be shown to contradict himself or say something paradoxical; or when he can answer only sophistically. Otherwise it fails, for the hearer cannot follow many questions.

scenes.title: How to Answer
scenes.summary: Answer ambiguous questions with distinctions and apparent contradictions with the solution at once. When the conclusion is put as a question, give the reason, as Sophocles answered Pisander about the Four Hundred and the Laconian ephor answered his auditor; and do not ask one question too many.

scenes.title: The Laughable
scenes.summary: Jests have their use in debate: Gorgias was right that one should spoil the opponents' seriousness with laughter and their laughter with seriousness. The kinds of the laughable are in the books on poetics; irony befits a free man better than buffoonery, for the ironist jokes for his own sake, the buffoon for another's.
